challenge.title: Early Resistance Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: five clue-and-conclusion decisions and five matching tasks. Choose both the supporting clue and its conclusion for each evidence decision. Get at least 7 activities correct. All supplied clues are available without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Early Resistance Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all five Chapter 12 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful comparison of causes, regional cases, participation, outcomes and remembrance.

evidence.question: A request was submitted. Which clue checks the claim that every demand was granted?
choices: Seeking changed terms does not prove that demands were granted
Every request succeeds
All requests are uprisings
A request ends all colonial rule
evidence.explanation: A petition is an action. Whether its demands were granted needs evidence of the result.

evidence.question: The selected uprisings started in different years. Which clue checks whether their order proves they worked together?
choices: Chronological order alone does not prove coordination
Earlier dates prove one shared plan
All movements began together
Every later event had the same cause
evidence.explanation: Ordering events helps comparison. It does not establish a shared plan or a causal link.

evidence.question: A pupil uses 1744-1829 as the founders certain lifespan. Which clue directly checks this?
choices: These are movement dates
These are certain birth and death dates
Every leader lived for the whole movement
All revolts lasted the same time
evidence.explanation: The dates belong to the movement. They do not establish the lifespan of its founder.

evidence.question: A source describes resistance spreading. Which clue checks whether every affected resident joined?
choices: Affected residents and participants are not automatically the same people
All affected residents joined
Only leaders can be affected
A place name gives every residents motive
evidence.explanation: Reach and participation are different questions. Joining needs evidence about people and actions.

evidence.question: The Basi paintings received recognition in 2009. Which clue checks whether this proves an immediate victory?
choices: Later recognition differs from an immediate outcome
Recognition proves every demand was won in 1807
The revolt happened in 2009
The paintings are photographs of a victory
evidence.explanation: Later cultural recognition concerns remembrance. It does not establish the outcome of the revolt.

matching.question: Match each part of an investigation with its meaning.
pairs: A concern about treatment or conditions
What people did about a concern
matching.explanation: Separate the reported problem, the action and its supported result.

matching.question: Match the selected regional cases with their settings.
matching.explanation: Keep each named case attached to its own place and period.

matching.question: Match each lesson clue to the case or idea it concerns.
pairs: Association linked with Apolinario de la Cruz
Local organization continued beyond its founder
Religious practice and political authority can connect
matching.explanation: Specific institutions and concerns help explain a case without assigning one belief to everyone.

matching.question: Match each participation question with the evidence it needs.
matching.explanation: Leadership, participation and being affected can overlap, but are not identical.

matching.question: Match each Basi timeline date with the right stage.
matching.explanation: An event, its representation and later recognition belong to different times.
